To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of an ortho-substituted phenyl ring in the 2- and/or 12-position of dibenzo[a, g]quinolizinium compounds increases antibacterial potency and disrupts FtsZ function.
2- and/or 12-bipenyl substituted dibenzo[ag]quinolizinium derivatives are highly potent antibacterial agents that act as enhancers on the FtsZ polymerization.
2- or12-biphenyldibenzo[a,g] quinolizin-7ium derivatives are potent antibiotics against S. aureus and E. faecalis and that these compounds act as FtsZ selfpolymerization enhancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new series of substituted dibenazo[a,g]quinolinium derivatives, which are potent inhibitors of bacterial growth, and which act as enhancers for FtsZ polymerization.
the development of new antibacterial agents with novel modes of action.
the discovery of novel antibacterial agents with the potential for the treatment of drug-resistant infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antibacterial activity of the dibenzo[a, g]quinolizinium derivatives is not only due to the inhibition of FtsZ function.

the presence of an electron-donating group at either the 12- or 2-position of dibenzo[a, g]quinolizinium salts enhances antibacterial activity and FtsZ self-association, while an electron-withdrawing group at the 2-position of a dibenzo[a g]quinolizinium salt enhances FtsZ self association without increasing antibacterial potency.
the 2- and the 12-bipheyl substituents in dibenzo[a, g]quinolizinium derivatives are able to increase their antibacterial activity by enhancing FtsZ self-assembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of an appropriately placed aromatic substituent in dibenzo[a, g]quinolizinium derivatives is a key factor in determining their antibacterial properties and that these derivatives may be considered as a novel class of FtsZ-targeted antibiotics.
dibenzo[a, g]quinolizin derivatives are a new class of antibiotics that act by disrupting the function of FtsZ.
the 2- and/or 12-bipphenyl dibenzo[ag]quinolizin derivatives are promising antibacterial agents that disrupt FtsZ function.

the presence of the biphenyl substituents at either the 1-, 2-, or 12-position in these compounds enhances antibacterial activity by increasing the potency of these FtsZ inhibitors.
the 2- and/or 12-bipheyl substituents in dibenzo[a, g]quinolizinium salts are essential for the disruption of bacterial cell division and the antibacterial activity of these molecules.
